info.title: API.SH: Substack
info.description: The Substack API from API.SH: public Substack data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A Substack leaderboard for a category: rank, publication (name, URL, logo, description), author, subscriber figures and bestseller tier. Paid ranks the bestsellers; trending (also accepted as rising) ranks the fastest-growing publications. Top 100 per category, 25 per page; pass `next_page` back as `page`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/substack-leaderboard

parameters.description: Category slug such as technology, business, culture, finance, food, sports or science, or its numeric id.

get.description:
A Substack newsletter: name, description, author, subscriber band, paid plans, podcast, sections and contributors. Works with substack.com subdomains and custom domains. `has_recommendations` says whether it recommends other publications; `recommendations=true` adds `recommendations`: the publications it recommends (name, URL, description, logo, author, language, paid flag, the recommending blurb and date). Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/substack-publication

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Publication URL, custom domain or substack subdomain.

parameters.name: recommendations
parameters.description: true adds the publications this one recommends (default false).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
